summary: Discovery call to evaluate Redwood for embeddings + reranking. Customer runs product search and recommendations, currently using hybrid BM25 + embeddings with Redis Vector. Key concerns: throughput (100-500 RPS), index dimensionality, storage cost, hybrid search, data residency and SOC2/KMS. Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment tradeoffs; agreed to run a 1M-vector benchmark and follow with technical deep dive.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-30
Time: 4:00 PM PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Mark Reynolds (Redwood AE), Aisha Patel (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (Silverpine Head of Data), Priya Singh (Eng Manager), Liam O'Connor (CTO)

[00:00] Mark: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, I'm Mark from Redwood, this is Aisha our solutions engineer. Um, just to kick off, can you tell us a bit about the problem you're solving with embeddings/rerank?

[00:18] Carlos: Yeah hi, thanks. So Silverpine runs a product search and recommendations stack, we currently use a hybrid approach, BM25 in Elastic for recall then we do an embed-based rerank using Redis Vector. The rerank's improving relevance but we're hitting cost and latency issues at peak.

[00:34] Priya: And to add, our traffic profile is spiky - holiday windows can push us to ~400 RPS for search endpoints for a few hours. We care about 95th p99 latency for rerank stage, ideally under 100ms extra.

[00:50] Mark: Got it. Do you manage your own Redis cluster or use a managed Redis vector offering?

[00:57] Carlos: It's self-managed on k8s, we've tuned a bit but ops cost is getting high. We also maintain an offline embedding pipeline - currently using a 768-dim model (open-source) which seems ok but we're evaluating larger dims for better recall.

[01:16] Aisha: Okay, good context. A few quick Qs: what's your current index size, ballpark? How many vectors and avg dims?

[01:24] Carlos: We're at ~8 million vectors overall but the search shard we care about is about 1.2 million. Dimensionality 768 today, considering moving to 1024 for some categories.

[01:35] Liam: Our main criteria: cost per query, predictable latency at scale, and the ability to run private deployments if needed for certain merchants with strict data residency.

[01:46] Mark: Excellent. I'll walk through how Redwood typically fits these use cases — quick note, I'll be a bit fuzzy on some internal names, transcription might flip bits, but Aisha can jump in with the technical.

[01:58] Mark: For embeddings + rerank we see two common patterns: 1) host embeddings in a vector DB (managed or self-hosted) and call Redwood Hosted or Dedicated to run the embedding model and/or retriever; or 2) Redwood handles only the rerank model and routing while customers keep vector DB. We support direct integrations with Redis, Pinecone, Weaviate, Milvus, etc.

[02:22] Priya: How does Redwood handle throughput? If we send 400 concurrent rerank requests, do you batch them? We can't break the latency SLO.

[02:32] Aisha: Yes, our runtime supports workload-aware batching and can be tuned with per-route batching, but batching trades throughput for added latency. For rerank flows we often enable small micro-batches (batch sizes 8-32) and use async prefix caching where applicable. For dedicated pools, you can get predictable GPU capacity and autoscaling policies.

[02:54] Carlos: When you say dedicated pools, do you mean Redwood Dedicated? We're trying to understand hosted vs dedicated vs private.

[03:02] Mark: Exactly. Hosted is our multi-tenant API — fastest to start. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity and predictable throughput with an SLA. Private is VPC or on-prem deployment for customers needing more network isolation or regulatory controls.

[03:15] Liam: Any customers running private on-prem for PCI or data residency?

[03:21] Aisha: Yes, we have a few enterprise customers on VPC and some on-prem installs. We integrate with KMS/HSM for key management and provide audit logs. There are some operations differences but the API surface is consistent across modes.

[03:36] Priya: Regarding index integration — if we keep Redis for ANN, will Redwood call Redis directly or do you recommend moving to a managed vector DB?

[03:45] Aisha: We support calling your vector DB directly from the application or from Redwood compute via connectors. Many customers keep their existing vector DB and use Redwood for model inference + rerank to reduce migration friction. That said, managed vector DBs can simplify ops and sometimes give better replication/latency characteristics.

[04:05] Carlos: We're concerned about storage cost at 1.2M vectors when we increase dims to 1024; any thoughts on quantization or lower-dim models?

[04:13] Aisha: Right — we often recommend model/quantization tradeoffs. For many ecom use cases, 384-768 dims are sweet spots. If you move to 1024 you can use int8 or gptq-style quantization in the vector store or at inference time to reduce storage and memory. Redwood Optimize also provides recommendations per workload.

[04:33] Mark: Also, rerank often benefits more from a higher-quality contextual model rather than just raw dimensionality. So sometimes switching to a slightly better embedder at 768 dims beats a naive jump to 1024. We can surface model-level A/B evals.

[04:48] Priya: Makes sense. For hybrid search, we currently do BM25 then top-100 embed rerank. Do you have guidance on top-K vs recall/latency tradeoffs?

[04:58] Aisha: Typical pattern: BM25 to 500 then embedding rerank on top-100 is common. If you want p99 latency under 100ms for rerank you'll likely aim for rerank candidate sets of 50-100 with a tuned embed model and limited batch size. We can run benchmarks to find the sweet spot.

[05:18] Carlos: For the benchmark, we'd like to measure recall@10/100, p95/p99 latency for rerank stage, and cost per 1k queries. Also memory pressure on vector store.

[05:28] Mark: Good — we usually do a 1M-vector benchmark for production-like signals. Aisha will draft the plan.

[05:34] [speaker 1]: Uh, sorry interrupt, quick question on real-time vs offline embeddings?

[05:38] Carlos: We do offline batch embeddings nightly and some near‑real-time for new products.

[05:43] Aisha: That's fine. Redwood supports both — you can push embeddings to your vector DB or have Redwood compute embeddings on the fly via API. If you want lower cost you precompute and store vectors; for fresh content you can compute just-in-time.

[05:57] Priya: About security, we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and KMS for encryption at rest. Is that covered?

[06:06] Mark: Yes, we are SOC2 compliant, support SAML SSO and RBAC. For private/VPC customers we can integrate with customer KMS or HSM. We'll share our security datasheet.

[06:18] Liam: Any gotchas around audit logs and deletion for GDPR?

[06:23] Aisha: We provide audit logs and retention configuration. For hosted customers we have controls for data retention and purging; for dedicated/private you can enforce your own retention via config. We'll include retention options in the SSO/security pack.

[06:36] Carlos: On latency, do you support on-prem colocation near our region? We have EU merchants and US merchants with different residency rules.

[06:45] Mark: Yes, you can choose deployments in different regions or use dedicated capacity in US/EU. For strict residency we'd recommend private VPC or on-prem.

[06:55] Priya: If we start with hosted for benching and then migrate to dedicated, what's the typical migration complexity?

[07:03] Aisha: The API is consistent. Migration is mostly operational: moving to reserved capacity and flipping endpoints. We help with model pinning and can run canary rollouts. There may be tuning for autoscaling policies but functionally it's straightforward.

[07:18] Mark: Any competitors you're evaluating?

[07:21] Liam: Yeah, Pinecone and managed Redis Vector, also some teams looked at Elastic's new vector capabilities.

[07:28] Mark: Great — we can share some benchmark comparatives and customer references.

[07:33] Carlos: About cost — can you ballpark what 100-500 RPS looks like cost-wise for ded deploy? We're thinking 3-5 GPUs reserved maybe?

[07:44] Aisha: Cost varies by model and quantization, but for rerank workloads you can often hit 100s of RPS on a single high-throughput GPU with batching and optimized kernels. Dedicated pool sizing depends on latency targets and model size; we'll propose tiered commit options in the pricing doc.

[07:59] Priya: Ok. For the benchmark plan, what do you need from us?

[08:04] Aisha: We'll need a sample dataset (Carlos mentioned 100k sample), queries and expected relevance judgments or click logs, target latency SLO, and any privacy constraints. We'll propose test vectors for 1M-scale run.

[08:16] Carlos: We can share a 100k sample CSV with ids, precomputed embeddings (if you want), and query set. We'll need to scrub PII.

[08:25] Mark: Perfect. Next steps recap: we'll send pricing + security docs, Aisha will send benchmark plan, and we'll schedule a technical deep dive to actually run the 1M-vector test.

[08:35] Liam: Sounds good. Timeline — we ideally want pilots by mid-December.

[08:39] Mark: Noted. We'll aim to get the pricing and benchmark plan out in 2-3 business days.

[08:45] Priya: One more smaller Q — do you support hybrid search where you can do BM25 on Elastic and then do vector similarity with Redwood compute in a single call?

[08:55] Aisha: We don't push BM25 itself into our runtime typically; recommended pattern is BM25 in Elastic to get candidates then call Redwood or your reranker. You can orchestrate it so it's effectively a single logical flow with minimal extra latency. We also have SDK examples for doing that.

[09:12] Carlos: Alright, thanks. We'll share sample and set up the deep dive.

[09:18] Mark: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and the benchmark plan.

[09:24] [end]
